title: BTEC HNC Electrical and Electronic Engineering for England (2024) — Unit 4019

handoff.scope: Inventory and generation/extraction requirements only. No symbol geometry, device models, footprints or application subfolder feature is implemented.
handoff.folder_semantics: folder is a proposed slash-separated logical path, not a claim of support in the current TinyCAD library browser.
handoff.source_document_base: All source_document paths are relative to the repository root, including in standalone library files.
handoff.identity: id is stable within a library; extraction may deduplicate by canonical_symbol_id, but each library is complete and permits independent duplicate assets.
handoff.pin_contract: Logical terminal numbers and signal names are not physical package pinouts. Resolve real package pins from an authoritative device reference before generating package-specific symbols.
handoff.conventions: Prefer IEC/UK teaching symbols. Power pins and polarity should remain explicit. Built-in instruments and probes are already provided and are excluded from symbol generation.
handoff.existing_tools: existing_tools and existing_tool_ids refer to supplied non-library tools, not generation requirements. Never recreate these as library symbols.
handoff.inventory_not_bom: One record per reusable symbol type, not per component instance. A bridge can be assembled from repeated diode/resistor symbols. Different resistance/capacitance values are properties, not separate symbols.
handoff.model_warning: Every record is marked not ready to simulate from this manifest. A successful extraction of artwork does not establish a valid model, mapping or instrument implementation.
handoff.optionality: experiment_symbol_ids are a coverage set of proposed implementations and comparisons, not a minimal mandatory BOM; common support symbols and explicitly optional additions are separately identified.

experiments.title: Nodal and loop checks
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose a multi-branch DC network, predict node potentials and signed currents, then compare simulation residuals with hand calculations.

experiments.title: Source superposition
experiments.catalogue_description: Solve a two-source circuit with each independent source deactivated in turn. Compare the sum of voltage/current contributions with the complete circuit. Do not sum power contributions as though power were linear.

experiments.title: Thevenin and Norton equivalents
experiments.catalogue_description: Obtain an equivalent at a selected port, then compare original and equivalent circuits under several finite loads. Avoid using a physical short as a measurement method.

experiments.title: Maximum power transfer
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary a resistor load against a source with explicit resistance. Compare load power and efficiency; maximum delivered power is not maximum efficiency.

experiments.title: Dividers and measurement loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare loaded/unloaded divider outputs and introduce finite meter input resistance. Quantify the measurement's influence.

experiments.title: Sinusoidal measurements
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare peak, RMS, frequency and phase using complete captured cycles. State whether an offset is included in the chosen RMS quantity.

experiments.title: RC and RL impedance
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep frequency and compare the magnitude/phase of voltage and current with calculated impedances. Include source resistance and coil resistance where appropriate.

experiments.title: First-order transient response
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture RC and RL responses to a step. Change one component at a time and compare fitted time constants with the declared circuit.

experiments.title: RLC resonance and damping
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare time-domain decay with frequency response for different resistances. Measure resonance, bandwidth and Q using a stated criterion.

experiments.title: Passive filter response
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare RC low-pass/high-pass networks with the same source and load. Relate AC response to pulse-shape changes from transient runs.

experiments.title: Power factor in a small RLC load
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare average instantaneous power with apparent power calculated from RMS readings. Export values for complex-power calculations if required.

experiments.title: Half/full-wave rectification and smoothing
experiments.catalogue_description: Use low-voltage sources and explicit diode mappings. Vary load/capacitance and compare ripple and mean output. Treat transformer input as a declared source unless a suitable coupled model is supplied.

experiments.title: Diode and Zener behaviour
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep current-limited circuits and compare operating voltage and dissipation. A Zener model must include the intended breakdown characteristic.

experiments.title: LED operating conditions
experiments.catalogue_description: Evaluate limiting resistors for several supplies using an identified LED model. Predict electrical current, not luminous intensity.

experiments.title: BJT switch and amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare switching and small-signal operation of a chosen transistor. Record DC bias before measuring gain and output range.

experiments.title: JFET/MOSFET comparison
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare gate-controlled current using appropriate models and separately stated operating conditions. Do not infer an interchangeable pinout or threshold.

experiments.title: Amplifier source/load interaction
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary source and load resistances around a prepared amplifier model. Measure gain and bandwidth under each condition.

experiments.title: Introductory op-amp feedback circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose a simple inverting/non-inverting stage and compare predicted gain with captures. Supply rail limits and a model adequate to the measurement.

experiments.title: Voltage logic and simple gate networks
experiments.catalogue_description: Verify small combinational functions and state the logic-level conventions. Use appropriate gate models; neither firmware nor HDL execution is implied.

experiments.title: Signal-chain and test-plan drawing
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw a sensor-equivalent source, conditioner and receiving stage, with test points and loading assumptions. The physical sensor and any PLC program remain outside the simulation.
